subject: Blended billing pilot + data minimization POC — scope & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Ramos <laura@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: ops@acme-analytics.com
Date: Tue, 6 May 2025 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Blended billing pilot + data minimization POC — scope & next steps

Hi all,

Following up from last week's sync — Acme is seeing sharp retention-driven spend on Datadog and Sentry and asked if we can propose a blended billing pilot that pairs a short retention/data-minimization POC with a commercial credit structure across their three vendors (Datadog, Grafana Cloud, Sentry).

High-level ask: can Redwood run a 6-week pilot that:
- Measures measurable token/log/metric reduction (goal: 25–40% ingest reduction) via targeted retention policies + prefix/KV caching for the same application traffic
- Provides a temporary blended credit that offsets incremental charges across vendors so Acme can evaluate unit economics without immediate multi-vendor contract changes
- Delivers a small set of SLI measurements (ingest rate, tail-query latency, query cost delta) and a final recommendation (keep, tier, or offload)

Attachments: pilot-scope.pdf (proposal), usage-baseline.csv (Acme-provided baseline).

Questions I have for internal owners:
1) Monica — procurement: what approvals/contract addenda are required to apply credits that offset third-party vendor overages for a pilot? Is a PO or MSA amendment required?
2) Marcus — engineering: rough feasibility for instrumenting an automatic retention pilot and a sampling rule on the Grafana/Datadog side; can we do lightweight traffic tagging to measure before/after without major infra changes?
3) Marissa — finance: do we need a formal accounting treatment for credits vs. discounts (revenue recognition/expensing)?

Next steps: if internal greenlight, I'd like a short kickoff with Acme later this week to lock scope and a target start date (ideally 5/12). Laura, are you still OK with that cadence?

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter | Strategic GTM 
Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Ramos <laura@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: ops@acme-analytics.com
Date: Tue, 6 May 2025 12:30:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Blended billing pilot + data minimization POC — scope & next steps

Thanks Ben — this looks like a practical approach. A few procurement items to flag up front:

- Contract mechanism: for a short pilot we typically issue a Statement of Work (SOW) or a signed Pilot Addendum under the existing MSA. That lets us define credit mechanics and the pilot start/end date without full contract renegotiation.
- Marketplace considerations: if Acme wants us to route credits through AWS/GCP marketplace SKUs (for simplicity on their PO side), we need to confirm the vendor (Datadog/Grafana) supports marketplace adjustments; that can slow the timeline by ~2 weeks.
- Billing true-up cadence: suggest monthly true-ups during pilot and a final reconciliation within 30 days. Finance will need a PO referencing DEAL-4392.

Marissa — FYI on accounting/fronting credits; I can draft a Pilot Addendum template for legal review.
Marcus — can you confirm runbook tasks and any risk of query regressions if we implement aggressive retention early in the pilot?

Ben — if Acme needs PO-driven accounting, request that now so we can align procurement lead times.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Head of Procurement Operations

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Ramos <laura@acme-analytics.com>

Date: Wed, 7 May 2025 08:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Blended billing pilot + data minimization POC — scope & next steps

Ben / team — technical recap and recommended minimal scope for a low-risk POC: 

1) Scope (6 weeks):
  - Week 0: baseline ingest + query profiling (we already have the CSV — thanks)
  - Week 1–3: non-invasive sampling & tag-based retention rules (no schema change)
  - Week 4–5: KV cache + short TTL for specific hot prefixes (targeting trace/log-heavy endpoints)
  - Week 6: post-change baseline + regression analysis

2) Risk mitigations:
  - Start with read-only sampling flags for 48 hours to validate signal before applying retention policies
  - Canary retention changes to a single service until we confirm no query regressions

3) Measurement plan: ingest reduction %, median/tail query latency, failed query rate, and sample-level fidelity loss (to measure functional impact).

I attached retention-tech-notes.md with example Grafana/Loki sampling rules and a Datadog archive/rollup approach. Rough engineering estimate: 3–5 engineer-days total to instrument the POC (small infra/devops effort).

Marissa — please confirm which GL code we should use for pilot credits (we can tag expenses to the DEAL-4392 project).

If this looks good I can draft a short runbook and a checklist for the kickoff.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Platform Engineer

Thanks, everyone — Acme is excited to proceed. A few items from our side:

- PO: I'll ask procurement to raise a PO referencing DEAL-4392 this afternoon; expect it by EOD Friday.
- Start date: 5/12 works for us. We prefer the pilot credit to be documented in an addendum rather than a marketplace pass-through (marketplace adds extra ops on our end).
- Legal/redlines: please send the Pilot Addendum template to legal@acme-analytics.com and I'll fast-track a review.

Also, would you please include a DocuSign link for the addendum? That will speed signature and allow our procurement to allocate credits to the right budget line.

Looking forward to the kickoff — Laura
